title: MA.32: a large negative breast-cancer trial despite metabolic effects

Q01.answer: Test adjunctive metformin for invasive disease-free survival after operable breast cancer. Final primary population hormone-receptor positive after planned futility assessment of receptor-negative disease. Recurrence, new invasive cancer or death. Subgroup analyses cannot replace the primary result.

Q02.answer: Adults 18–74 with high-risk nonmetastatic breast cancer without diabetes. Canada, US, UK and Switzerland; complete resection and standard cancer therapy. 3649 randomized: 1824 metformin and 1825 placebo; primary ER/PgR-positive group 1268 and 1265. Almost all participants were women.

Q03.answer: Apotex metformin and matching placebo. Oral 850 mg daily for four weeks then twice daily, intended five years. Standard endocrine, chemotherapy, radiation and targeted therapy as indicated. Median primary follow-up 96.2 months. Not metformin monotherapy for cancer.

Q04.answer: Identical-appearing placebo. 1:1 minimization, balanced by center and stratified by receptors, BMI and chemotherapy. Computer-based allocation procedure described as minimization with equal probabilities. Double-blind. Concurrent enrollment 2010–2013, data cutoff October 2020. Randomization and long follow-up are major strengths.

Q05.answer: Primary invasive disease-free survival; OS and recurrence endpoints secondary. Centrally verified events and time-to-event analysis. Final follow-up approximately eight years. Clinical cancer outcomes. Design targeted about four percentage points at five years, based on investigator consensus. Metabolic improvements are not the same endpoint.

Q06.answer: Primary events 234/1268 metformin versus 231/1265 placebo. 18.5% versus 18.3% crude observed event proportions. Incidence 2.78 versus 2.74 per 100 patient-years; HR 1.01, CI 0.84–1.21, P=.93. OS HR 1.10, CI 0.86–1.41; receptor-negative iDFS HR 1.01, CI 0.79–1.30. No primary benefit; exploratory HER2-positive signal lacked a significant HER2-by-treatment interaction. Do not present HER2 subgroup benefit as established.

Q07.answer: All randomized participants included in assigned-group analyses. Missing dates imputed within known intervals; time-to-event censoring used. Final-year reported continuation 64.3% metformin versus 70.9% placebo in the defined eligible subset. Receptor-negative participants stopped study drug for futility while blinded follow-up continued. ITT, with prespecified/supervised change in primary population. Individual participant. Discontinuation affects exposure but does not create a second trial.

Q08.answer: All grade 3+ events while taking study drug; treatment-related events thereafter. Full randomized groups 1824 and 1825; exact safety count/percentage reconciliation remains needed. Main text reports 391 (21.5%) versus 328 (17.5%) grade 3+ nonhematologic events; the latter count does not reproduce the stated percentage with n=1825. Toxicity could lead to dose reduction/discontinuation. Intended five years of exposure, with later follow-up. Guide describes greater reported severe toxicity without deriving a precise absolute difference from discordant numbers.

Q09.answer: Strong blinded large RCT; incomplete drug continuation and changes after interim analysis matter. Randomization protects primary comparison; exploratory subgroups remain vulnerable to chance. A full original protocol/SAP was not recovered. The two acquired metabolic-companion supplements are an interaction table and reporting summary, not the protocol/SAP. Primary alpha .037; secondary and subgroup findings exploratory. CI excludes the originally targeted large relative benefit, but smaller effects remain possible. Abstract diarrhea percentages conflict with Results; placebo grade 3+ count and percentage conflict; no silent numeric repair. Use verified primary outcome rather than discordant harm percentages for precise effect calculations.

Q10.answer: High-risk operable breast cancer without diabetes. Five-year intended adjunctive regimen. Does not support adding metformin to prevent invasive recurrence. Cannot determine diabetes-specific benefit or every molecular subgroup. Do not use a cancer null result to advise stopping diabetes care.

Q11.answer: CCTG MA.32 single randomized family. COND-C15-MA32-METABOLIC reports six-month metabolic markers. Companion participants overlap; no extra trial count. Current source reconciliation, not an exhaustive breast-cancer review. Metabolic change is not independent survival replication.

Q12.answer: Pamela Goodwin, Bingshu Chen and collaborators. CCTG international trial. Cancer charities and public research grants; CCTG trial sponsorship. Apotex donated metformin and placebo. Multiple investigators disclosed consulting, grants and industry employment/advisory relationships. The main result is assessed from design and data, not sponsor labels.

Q13.answer: Published JAMA 2022, DOI 10.1001/jama.2022.6147. Full main article acquired; primary table assessed. Full original protocol/SAP not recovered; the metabolic-companion interaction table and reporting summary do not replace it. NCT01101438 identified; no complete historical registry audit. No formal correction located in bounded current search; internal numerical discrepancies retained. November 3–4, 2026. Do not label unresolved source inconsistencies corrected.

Q14.answer: Recurrence prevention versus metabolic improvement. Strong direct evidence against the proposed large general adjuvant benefit. Author conclusion and primary results agree; favorable exploratory subgroups remain hypotheses. Keep primary and exploratory findings visibly separate.

Q15.answer: Metformin did not improve invasive disease-free survival in the primary population. Smaller effects and prospectively defined subgroups remain separate questions. Replicated subgroup-specific randomized evidence with clinical outcomes would be required. Improved insulin or weight measures alone are insufficient.

appraisal: Large, blinded randomized evidence with long follow-up is negative for the primary clinical endpoint. Metabolic companion results and exploratory HER2 findings do not overturn it. Discordant adverse-event numbers are explicitly retained rather than silently recalculated.
